facts.text: A hazard is a potential source of harm; harm is the injury or damage that occurs; risk combines the probability of harm with its severity.
facts.quote: A hazard is something that could hurt someone, harm is the injury or damage that actually happens, and risk is how likely the harm is, combined with how bad it would be.

facts.text: The machinery standard ISO 12100 defines hazard, harm and risk as used in safety engineering.
facts.quote: Safety engineering uses the three words in exactly this way, and the machinery standard ISO 12100 defines them.

facts.text: Many standards include damage to property or the environment within harm, in addition to physical injury or damage to health.
facts.quote: Harm is physical injury or damage to health; many standards add damage to property or the environment.

facts.text: For a worker behind a reversing haul truck near a dump point, collision risk depends on exposure to reversing trucks and the severity of being run over; the passage describes being run over by a 100 ton truck as almost always fatal.
facts.quote: The risk depends on how often people are behind reversing trucks (the exposure) and on the severity, which for a 100 ton truck is almost always fatal.

facts.text: The booklet quotes a United States figure of about 13 mine workers killed each year by being run over or pinned by mobile mining equipment.
facts.quote: The booklet quotes a United States figure of about 13 mine workers killed each year by being run over or pinned by mobile mining equipment [Chapter 10].

facts.text: Automatic braking can create new hazards when a loaded machine stops hard on a slope, under a suspended load, beside a trailer or in front of a following machine, even if braking reduces another risk.
facts.quote: an automatic brake that stops a loaded machine hard on a slope, under a suspended load, beside a trailer or in front of a following machine is itself a hazard [Chapters 1, 9].

facts.text: The booklet recommends separately analyzing failure to brake when required and braking when not required or when braking itself is dangerous.
facts.quote: two hazards must be analyzed separately: the system fails to brake when it should, and the system brakes when it should not or when braking is itself dangerous [Chapter 3].

facts.text: Risk is never zero; risk reduction aims to reach a level accepted by someone with authority.
facts.quote: Risk is never zero; the aim is to bring it down to a level that someone with authority accepts.

facts.text: Every requirement, test and acceptance criterion in the braking validation plan should trace back to a named hazard.
facts.quote: Every requirement, test and acceptance criterion in the plan should trace back to a named hazard.

facts.text: The booklet warns that the braking-intervention hazard analysis must be approved before the prototype arrives; otherwise the four months will be spent debating dangers rather than gathering evidence.
facts.quote: the hazard analysis for the braking intervention must be approved before the prototype arrives, or the four months will be spent debating what is dangerous instead of gathering evidence [Chapter 13].
